## The lost plants of Galiano Island

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="lost"}
This gallery shows `<span class="mxcw-lost-count">@{count}</span>`{=html} native species once reported for Galiano Island, which have not been seen in recent decades. Some may be lost *to us*—overlooked, forgotten, or waiting to be rediscovered. Others may be lost *because of us*, through impacts like habitat change or the introduction of invasive species.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Pick a plant from the gallery</span> to turn it over and read its curatorial notes. From there you can follow it to its records in the Atlas, or add your own notes in Living Data. Then join local naturalists and community members on a search for it through the
[Biodiversity Galiano Island](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/biodiversity-galiano-island)
project on iNaturalist.
:::

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="confirmed" hidden="hidden"}
These native species were known to the island's earlier botanists, and have been **seen again** since 2004. They are the enduring core of its native flora—though being found again is no promise of security, and some now survive in only one or two places.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Pick a plant from the gallery</span> to turn it over and read its curatorial notes, then follow it to its records in the Atlas to see where it persists, or add your own notes in Living Data.
:::

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="new" hidden="hidden"}
These native species were **first reported** for Galiano Island since 2004. Some were surely here all along, overlooked by earlier botanists or confused with their relatives; others may be newly arrived, or newly told apart by taxonomists.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Pick a plant from the gallery</span> to turn it over and read its curatorial notes, then follow it to its records in the Atlas, or add your own notes in Living Data.
:::

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="excluded" hidden="hidden"}
Not every plant reported for the island belongs on its checklist. These taxa are **excluded** from it: curators have judged some to be doubtful reports, others to be garden escapes that persist without establishing.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Pick a plant from the gallery</span> to turn it over and read the curators' reasoning. These notes show how the checklist was made, and where it remains open to question.
:::

Herbarium collections at the Royal BC Museum and UBC, and Harvey Janszen’s (2003) *Outer Gulf Islands Vascular Plant
Checklist*, provide the historical baseline for this atlas. Harvey passed away in 2021, and a community of naturalists
has since carried his work forward through [Biodiversity Galiano](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/biodiversity-galiano-island);
this atlas is a testament to that continuing legacy.
